title: Authorization ontology, resource graph, and guardrail matrix for RBAC v2
creator: Noah Patel
description: Design and deliver a canonical authorization ontology and resource graph that will be the single source-of-truth for RBAC v2 evaluation and for audit log enrichment. This ticket covers: resource taxonomy (tenant, org, project, model, deployment, route, dataset, secret), scope semantics (explicit grant, transitive/derived, ephemeral session grants), claim-to-role resolution (SAML/SCIM group mapping, OIDC claims), negative/deny semantics, admin guardrails (break-glass, emergency escrows, delegated admin), and the permissions matrix used by runtime policy evaluation and Console UI. Outputs: schema for resource graph, SQL migrations for new permission tables, evaluation pseudocode, telemetry contract for enriched audit events, and a guardrail matrix for administrators to reason about risk vs convenience.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical resource graph schema documented and reviewed (entities, edges, cardinality, tenancy annotations).
Permissions matrix CSV created showing 1) primitive actions, 2) resources they apply to, 3) default allow/deny, 4) requires explicit admin approval.
Claim-to-role mapping rules defined for SAML groups, SCIM, and OIDC; examples for common IdPs included.
Runtime evaluation algorithm (pseudocode) and evaluation order documented (direct grants -> scope inheritance -> transitive -> deny overrides).
Audit event enrichment spec produced (fields, example event, size budget) and agreed with Observability.
DB migration and API contract PRs opened and passing basic CI smoke tests.
Guardrail matrix reviewed with Security and PM; at least one canary rollout path defined for tenant migration.
tasks: Draft resource taxonomy and graph model (entity list + relations).
Enumerate primitive actions (read, write, manage, run, impersonate, escalate).
Map current roles to new permission primitives and flag gaps.
Define SAML/SCIM claim rules and example mappings for Okta/GSuite/Azure AD.
Write runtime evaluation pseudocode and complexity/batch/caching notes.
Sketch Console UI mapping for role editor and guardrail visualization.
Prepare DB migration plan and representational tables for audits.
Sync with Observability for audit event payload and retention implications.
Create migration playbook and canary rollout checklist.
decisions: Use an explicit, entity-centric resource graph (edges stored as adjacency list) instead of flat hierarchical path strings to allow multi-parent resources (decision 2025-02-20).

Permission evaluation order will be: explicit allow grants -> inherited/transitive grants -> ephemeral/session grants -> explicit deny (deny wins) to keep semantics simple for UI explanations (decision 2025-02-22).
SAML group mappings will be treated as first-class role assignments but require admin confirmation on first-seen mapping (prevents accidental privilege creep).
No runtime negative permissions for non-admin users in first phase; Deny semantics reserved for admin policies and customer-managed deny-lists to reduce evaluation complexity.
tradeoffs: Adjacency-list resource graph enables flexible relationships (datasets belonging to multiple projects) at the cost of more complex recursive queries during evaluation versus path-based approach.
Treating SAML groups as first-class simplifies onboarding but introduces a risk of over-privileging if group names are inconsistent; mitigated by admin-confirmation and audit alerts.
Deny semantics limited to admin policies reduces developer confusion but delays some security patterns for customers who need deny-by-default.
migration_plan: Phase 0: Read-only compatibility layer — build resource graph from existing role/permission tables and emit enriched audit events (no enforcement changes).
Phase 1: Opt-in enforcement for new roles on non-critical routes (canary customers) with monitoring for denied requests and false positives.
Phase 2: Full enforcement for new roles in runtime with a fallback 'legacy' flag per tenant for 30 days.
Rollback plan: toggle enforcement flag per tenant + automated script to rehydrate pre-migration role bindings.
test_plan: Unit tests for pseudocode evaluator covering: direct grants, inherited grants, transitive grants, deny precedence, and session grants.
Integration tests: end-to-end with SAML assert -> SCIM sync -> role assignment -> API request flows.
Load test: evaluate permission checks at 10k rps to validate caching strategy and latency impact.
Canary validation: run synthetic flows that exercise admin guardrails and ensure audit events are emitted and indexed.
notes: Resource graph canonical entities: tenant, org, project, team, model, deployment, route, dataset, secret, job.
Primitive actions considered: read, list, create, update, delete, manage, execute, impersonate, escalate, view_billing, manage_keys.
Telemetry contract draft: event_type, actor_id, actor_claims, action, resource_id, resource_path, resource_ancestry (ids), evaluation_trace, decision, policy_version. Payload target <= 2KB per event.
We need to coordinate with Console team for role editor UX; see design brief: drive.google.com/drive/fake-link-role-editor.
